segments.intent: Compare average body measurements across penguin species
segments.value:
```sql
SELECT species, COUNT(*) AS penguin_count, AVG(bill_length_mm) AS avg_bill_length_mm, AVG(bill_depth_mm) AS avg_bill_depth_mm, AVG(flipper_length_mm) AS avg_flipper_length_mm, AVG(body_mass_g) AS avg_body_mass_g FROM penguins GROUP BY species ORDER BY species
```

<details open><summary>Result</summary>

```
    species penguin_count avg_bill_length_mm avg_bill_depth_mm
1    Adelie           152           38.79139          18.34636
2 Chinstrap            68           48.83382          18.42059
3    Gentoo           124           47.50488          14.98211
  avg_flipper_length_mm avg_body_mass_g
1              189.9536        3700.662
2              195.8235        3733.088
3              217.1870        5076.016
```

</details>

segments.content:
Here are the main differences in average body measurements by species: | Species | Count | Avg bill length (mm) | Avg bill depth (mm) | Avg flipper length (mm) | Avg body mass (g) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Adelie | 152 | 38.8 | 18.3 | 190.0 | 3700.7 | | Chinstrap | 68 | 48.8 | 18.4 | 195.8 | 3733.1 | | Gentoo | 124 | 47.5 | 15.0 | 217.2 | 5076.0 | Key takeaways: - **Gentoo** penguins are the largest overall: they have the **longest flippers** and are **much heavier** than the other species. - **Adelie** penguins have the **shortest bills** and **shortest flippers**. - **Chinstrap** penguins have the **longest bills** on average. - **Bill depth** is where Gentoo stand out in the opposite direction: they have **noticeably shallower bills** than Adelie and Chinstrap. - **Adelie and Chinstrap** are fairly similar in **body mass**, but differ strongly in **bill length**: Chinstrap bills are much longer. These are species-level averages, so it’s worth checking the spread within each species before treating the differences as cleanly separated.
